title: Perfect tensor global sections preserve quasi-coherent derived limits
statement:
Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of algebraic spaces over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-trf-algebraic-space]. Quasi-compact means inverse images of quasi-compact spaces are quasi-compact, and quasi-separated means the relative diagonal is quasi-compact. Use the small etale structure sheaf, module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and quasi-coherent modules [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Write $C_X=D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ for the full subcategory of objects with quasi-coherent cohomology. Let $E\in C_X$ be perfect, meaning etale locally represented by a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free structure modules [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Use K-flat derived tensor [def-pc-kflat-complex] and K-injective derived global sections (a complex is K-injective if every map from an acyclic complex to it is null-homotopic) [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology], retaining the $A$-module action induced by $f$.
The functor
$$F_E:C_X\longrightarrow D(A),\qquad H\longmapsto R\Gamma(X,H\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}^{\mathbf L}E)$$
is exact and preserves products in the chosen indexing universe: the morphism $F_E(\prod_jH_j)\to\prod_jF_E(H_j)$ with components $F_E(\operatorname{pr}_j)$ is an isomorphism. The source product is taken in $C_X$. Consequently, applying $F_E$ to a product triangle
$$L\longrightarrow P\xrightarrow{1-s}P\longrightarrow L[1],\qquad P=\prod_{n\ge1}H_n,\quad\operatorname{pr}_ns=t_n\operatorname{pr}_{n+1},$$
for any countable tower $H_{n+1}\xrightarrow{t_n}H_n$ in $C_X$, gives a derived limit of the tower $(F_E(H_n),F_E(t_n))$ in $D(A)$ [def-weil-derived-limit]: with $c:F_E(P)\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_nF_E(H_n)$ the product comparison, $F_E(L)\xrightarrow{cF_E(p)}\prod_nF_E(H_n)\xrightarrow{1-s'}\prod_nF_E(H_n)\to F_E(L)[1]$ is distinguished, where $p:L\to P$ is the first arrow and $\mathrm{pr}_ns'=F_E(t_n)\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}$. In particular, for every derived limit $(R,p',\delta')$ of $(F_E(H_n),F_E(t_n))$ there is an isomorphism in $D(A)$,
$$F_E(L)\xrightarrow{\sim}R=R\varprojlim_nF_E(H_n),$$
whose composite with the $n$th projection $\mathrm{pr}_np'$ is $F_E(q_n)$, where $q_n=\mathrm{pr}_np:L\to H_n$ is the projection of the given triangle. The product comparison $c$ is natural in morphisms of the $H_j$ and in morphisms of perfect $E$. No surjectivity, module concentration, finite presentation, proper support, or nilpotent-ring-tower hypothesis on the $H_n$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0CX6 (lemma-compute-against-perfect), proof: the exact product-preserving global RHom functor commutes with derived limits, translated to perfect tensor global sections by the dual-perfect-complex identification. This node states that general functor assertion, not the infinitesimal perfectness conclusion.

proof.text: First construct ambient products, without asserting quasi-coherence. Use the small ringed model [def-sfb-space-small-ringed-model]. For any small family of module sheaves, the sectionwise product is a module sheaf: restrictions and scalar multiplication are coordinatewise, and compatible sections glue uniquely in each coordinate. Thus termwise products of complexes exist. By [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], represent each $H_j$ by a K-injective complex $I_j$. By [lem-pc-ringed-space-product-kinjective], $B=Q(\prod_j I_j)$ with its specified projections is the product of the $H_j$ in $D(\mathcal O_X)$. The cited statement is for an arbitrary abelian category and an arbitrary set, despite its title. Applying the same two statements to the one-object ringed site with ring $A$ proves existence of every small product in $D(A)$. Empty products give the zero object. No exactness of products of module sheaves is used.

source.place: Tag 0CX6, lemma-compute-against-perfect, proof, exact global Hom and derived limits paragraph; details in the auxiliary places stated in this step. derived.tex Tag 0BK6, lemma-product-K-injective; injectives.tex Tag 07D9, lemma-derived-products.

proof.text:
The relative hypotheses imply the qcqs hypotheses needed for [lem-sfb-space-derived-coherator-adjunction]. Apply the affine tests and base-change stability in [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests]; [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-source-products] also gives absolute quasi-separatedness from the quasi-separated morphism to the quasi-separated affine base. Quasi-compactness follows by applying quasi-compactness of $f$ to the affine target. For affine etale charts $U,V\to X$, the scheme $U\times_A V$ is affine, and $U\times_X V\to U\times_A V$ is the pullback of the relative diagonal; it is quasi-compact by quasi-separatedness of $f$. Thus the chart intersections are quasi-compact. Apply the cited adjunction $I_X\dashv DQ_X$. For the ambient product $B$ of step 1, put $P=DQ_XB$; its $j$th projection is the counit $I_XP\to B$ followed by the $j$th ambient projection. For every $T\in C_X$, the counit adjunction and the ambient product give
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{C_X}(T,P)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(I_XT,B)\cong\prod_j\operatorname{Hom}_{C_X}(T,H_j).$$
Both bijections are induced by these projections, so this is exactly the product universal property in $C_X$. This argument also covers the empty family.

source.place: Tag 0CX6, lemma-compute-against-perfect, proof, exact global Hom and derived limits paragraph; details in the auxiliary places stated in this step. spaces-perfect.tex Tag 0CR4, lemma-better-coherator.

proof.text:
Set $D=E^\vee$. By [lem-sfb-ringed-site-perfect-duality], $D$ is perfect and the canonical map $E\to D^\vee$ is invertible. Moreover $D$ belongs to $C_X$: on a strict-perfect chart, each term is a retract of a finite free module and hence quasi-coherent; kernels, images and cokernels remain quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits], so its cohomology is quasi-coherent, which is an etale-local condition. Apply the evaluation isomorphism of the duality lemma with first argument $D$ and second argument $H$. It identifies $H\otimes^{\mathbf L}E$ with $R\mathcal Hom(D,H)$, naturally in $H$. The final clause of [lem-sfb-ringed-site-global-rhom-derived-limits] therefore gives, for every integer $q$,
$$H^qF_E(H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(D,H[q])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{C_X}(D[-q],H).$$
All maps here retain the $A$-action. Only the cohomology-identification clause of the global-Hom node is used, not its assertion about ambient derived limits.

source.place: Tag 0CX6, lemma-compute-against-perfect, proof, exact global Hom and derived limits paragraph; details in the auxiliary places stated in this step. sites-cohomology.tex Tags 08JJ (lemma-dual-perfect-complex) and 0B6E (section-global-RHom).

proof.text: The functor is defined on $C_X$ because [lem-sfb-space-derived-qcoh-pullback-tensor] says that the derived tensor of two quasi-coherent derived objects is quasi-coherent. Choose a flat-term K-flat resolution of $E$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Then [lem-weil-pbc-kflat-fixed-tensor-triangulated] makes tensoring with this fixed resolution an exact functor, including its signed shift comparison and connecting maps. Global sections with its induced $A$-action is an additive functor from module sheaves to $A$-modules. Both categories admit K-injective resolutions by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], using the one-object site for $A$-modules. Thus [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated] makes its K-injective right derived functor exact. Composing these two exact functors and restricting to the full triangulated subcategory $C_X$ proves exactness of $F_E$.

source.place: Tag 0CX6, lemma-compute-against-perfect, proof, exact global Hom and derived limits paragraph; details in the auxiliary places stated in this step. sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YU, definition-derived-tor; right-derived triangulated structure in WeilConjectures/CategoryTheory/DerivedCategory/RightDerivedFunctor/Triangulated.lean, instances at lines 94-99.

proof.text:
In $D(A)$, [lem-sc-module-cup-homology-representability] identifies $H^q(N)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(A[-q],N)$, naturally in $N$. Consequently the product universal property, applied with test object $A[-q]$, gives
$$H^q(\prod_jN_j)\cong\prod_jH^q(N_j).$$
This is the map whose components are the cohomologies of the product projections. The family may be any small set, including the empty set. This uses representability, not a claim that ordinary sheaf products are exact.

source.place: Tag 0CX6, lemma-compute-against-perfect, proof, exact global Hom and derived limits paragraph; details in the auxiliary places stated in this step. derived.tex Tag 064B, lemma-morphisms-from-projective-complex, applied to the rank-one single complex; the product universal property.

proof.text:
Let $P=\prod_j^{C_X}H_j$ and let $c:F_E(P)\to\prod_jF_E(H_j)$ be the comparison specified in the statement. For every integer $q$, step 3 and the universal property of $P$ identify its source cohomology with
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{C_X}(D[-q],P)\cong\prod_j\operatorname{Hom}_{C_X}(D[-q],H_j)\cong\prod_jH^qF_E(H_j).$$
Step 5 identifies its target cohomology with the same product. Naturality of the step-3 identification shows that the $j$th component of $H^q(c)$ is precisely postcomposition with $\operatorname{pr}_j$. Thus $H^q(c)$ is an isomorphism for every $q$, and [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] implies that $c$ is an isomorphism. This proves preservation for every small family, not only for countable towers.

source.place: Tag 0CX6, lemma-compute-against-perfect, proof, exact global Hom and derived limits paragraph; details in the auxiliary places stated in this step. sites-cohomology.tex Tags 08JJ and 0B6E; derived.tex Tag 05RT, lemma-acyclic.

proof.text: The comparison is natural in the family: for maps $u_j:H_j\to H'_j$, both sides of the naturality square have $j$th component $F_E(u_j\operatorname{pr}_j)$. For a morphism $v:E\to E'$ of perfect objects, the transformation $F_E\to F_{E'}$ is induced by $1_H\otimes^{\mathbf L}v$. Tensor bifunctoriality makes its square with every $H$-projection commute. Hence both sides of the corresponding product-comparison square have the same $j$th component. The product universal property proves both squares commute, including for an empty family.

source.place: Tag 0CX6, lemma-compute-against-perfect, proof, exact global Hom and derived limits paragraph; details in the auxiliary places stated in this step. Product universal property and bifunctoriality of the derived tensor functor in the statement.

proof.text:
For the given tower put $Q=\prod_nF_E(H_n)$ and use the isomorphism $c:F_E(P)\to Q$ from step 6. Additivity and functoriality give, for every $n$,
$$\operatorname{pr}_n cF_E(s)=F_E(t_n\operatorname{pr}_{n+1})=F_E(t_n)\operatorname{pr}_{n+1}c.$$
Therefore $cF_E(1-s)c^{-1}=1-s'$, since the equality holds after every projection of $Q$. Exactness from step 4 sends the given product triangle to a distinguished triangle. Transport its two product vertices along $c$, and use the shift comparison of $F_E$ for the last arrow. This gives the distinguished triangle
$$F_E(L)\xrightarrow{cF_E(p)}Q\xrightarrow{1-s'}Q\longrightarrow F_E(L)[1].$$
By [def-weil-derived-limit] this is a derived limit of the image tower, with $n$th projection $F_E(\operatorname{pr}_np)=F_E(q_n)$.

source.place: Tag 0CX6, lemma-compute-against-perfect, proof, exact global Hom and derived limits paragraph; details in the auxiliary places stated in this step. derived.tex Tag 08TC, definition-derived-limit, and the TR1 closure under triangle isomorphisms.

proof.text: Let $(R,p',\delta')$ be any other specified derived limit of the image tower. Rotate its Roos triangle and that of step 8 so that both start with the same arrow $Q\xrightarrow{1-s'}Q$. Apply TR3 of [def-weil-triangulated-category] with the identity maps on these two vertices, then rotate back. It supplies $a:F_E(L)\to R$ completing the original triangles and satisfying $p'a=cF_E(p)$. Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-r-lim-levelwise-isomorphism] with the identity isomorphism on every object of the image tower: $a$ is an isomorphism. Composing the displayed equality with $\operatorname{pr}_n$ gives $\operatorname{pr}_np'a=F_E(q_n)$. Existence, rather than uniqueness or canonicity, is exactly what the statement requires. None of these steps used a surjectivity or finiteness condition on the tower.

It has no new nodes, the statement is unchanged and is not weakened, and proof_deps equals the union of the step uses. Source check: Stacks 0CX6 says RHom_X(E,-) on D_QCoh commutes with products and so with derived limits, then turns (1) into (2) via 08JJ; 0CR4 gives the coherator right adjoint. The nine steps follow that route. Step 1: ambient products from K-injective representatives through the small ringed model; 0BK6 holds for any abelian category. Step 2: qcqs of X follows from the affine tests, since U×_X V is a pullback of Δ_{X/A} over an affine. P = DQ_X(∏) has the product property in C_X. Step 3: D = E^∨ is perfect, lies in C_X by 03M1, and E⊗H ≅ RHom(D,H). Only the H^q-identification clause of the global-RHom node is used, not its strict-tower limit claim. Step 4: exactness from the fixed K-flat tensor and the right-derived functor of RΓ. Steps 5-6: H^q in D(A) is represented by A[-q], so H^q(c) is the identity on ∏H^qF_E(H_j); the cohomology criterion then makes c an isomorphism. Step 8: conjugating by c and applying TR1 gives the Roos triangle with projections F_E(q_n). Step 9: rotation plus TR3 gives (a,1,1), and the levelwise-isomorphism lemma with u_n = id makes a an isomorphism with pr_n p' a = F_E(q_n). Edge cases (empty family, singleton, E=0, unbounded objects, zero transitions) are fine. Batch 5: all six flagged citations reach sec-trace-formula only through def-trf-algebraic-space and other basic algebraic-space and quasi-coherence nodes, none of which is part of the trace formula or Poincaré duality, so this is not a RETURN. All seven split_report.tool_uses are generic tools and are accepted.
